sentences.en: What causes stress?
sentences.zh: 什么导致了压力？

sentences.en: Money?
sentences.zh: 金钱？

sentences.en: Work?
sentences.zh: 工作？

sentences.en: Illness?
sentences.zh: 疾病？

sentences.en: What about discrimination?
sentences.zh: 那歧视呢？

sentences.en: Nearly half of Americans report they have experienced a major form of discrimination.
sentences.zh: 近一半的美国人表示他们经历过某种主要的歧视。

sentences.en: These acts are associated with higher reported stress levels and poor health.
sentences.zh: 这些行为与较高的压力水平和较差的健康状况有关。

sentences.en: That's according to the latest Stress in America survey.
sentences.zh: 这是根据最新的“美国压力”调查得出的结论。

sentences.en: In this episode, we speak with a psychologist about how different groups respond to stress and how best to cope.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们采访了一位心理学家，探讨不同群体如何应对压力以及如何最好地处理压力。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton, and this is Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿，这是《心理学谈话》。

sentences.en: Lynn Bufka is Associate Executive Director for Practice Research and Policy at the American
sentences.zh: 琳恩·布夫卡是美国心理学会实践研究与政策部的副执行主任。

sentences.en: Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 心理学会。

sentences.en: She was on a panel of experts who developed APA's 2016 Stress in
sentences.zh: 她是制定美国心理学会2016年“美国压力”调查的专家组成员之一。

sentences.en: America survey.
sentences.zh: 调查。

sentences.en: A licensed psychologist, she is an expert in stress and mind-body health matters.
sentences.zh: 作为一名执业心理学家，她是压力和身心健康问题方面的专家。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Bufka.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，布夫卡博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: Let's get right into the focus of this year's Stress in America survey, which looks at the link between discrimination and stress.
sentences.zh: 让我们直接进入今年“美国压力”调查的焦点，即歧视与压力之间的联系。

sentences.en: According to the report, 69% of adults in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 根据报告，69%的美国成年人

sentences.en: report having experienced discrimination,
sentences.zh: 表示经历过歧视，

sentences.en: 61% saying they experience day-to-day discrimination.
sentences.zh: 61%的人表示他们经历过日常歧视。

sentences.en: When people are treated differently because of their race or sexual orientation or gender, for example, what effect does it have on their physical and mental health over time?
sentences.zh: 例如，当人们因为种族、性取向或性别而受到不同对待时，随着时间的推移，这对他们的身心健康有什么影响？

sentences.en: Well, when people are treated differently, ideally, you know, we recognize experiences of discrimination as being not about us and recognize it as actually being discrimination
sentences.zh: 嗯，当人们受到不同对待时，理想情况下，你知道，我们应该认识到歧视经历并非因我们而起，并认识到这实际上是歧视，

sentences.en: or understand it's the other person's problematic behavior.
sentences.zh: 或者理解这是对方的问题行为。

sentences.en: But when it happens repeatedly, that's really hard to do.
sentences.zh: 但当这种情况反复发生时，这真的很难做到。

sentences.en: We start to internalize.
sentences.zh: 我们开始内化。

sentences.en: Maybe there's something about us.
sentences.zh: 也许是我们自身有什么问题。

sentences.en: Maybe it's me that's causing this to happen or maybe there's something that's not quite right or it can pick away at your
sentences.zh: 也许是我导致了这种情况发生，或者也许有什么地方不太对劲，或者反复感到自己是这些事情的经历者、目标，会一点点侵蚀你的

sentences.en: self-esteem to repeatedly feel that you're the experience, the target of these things.
sentences.zh: 自尊心。

sentences.en: You may start believing negative things about yourself that are consistent with the discrimination or perhaps you'll even
sentences.zh: 你可能会开始相信关于自己的负面评价，这些评价与歧视相一致，或者你甚至会

sentences.en: behave differently or avoid situations, even if those are loved activities or possible job opportunities or
sentences.zh: 表现得不同，或者回避某些情况，即使那是你喜爱的活动、可能的工作机会或

sentences.en: interesting classes you might want to take just because you don't want to be potentially in a situation where you could be experiencing discrimination.
sentences.zh: 你可能想参加的有趣课程，仅仅因为你不想让自己处于可能遭受歧视的情况中。

sentences.en: Sometimes you might even do things like you in a situation, but you're less reserved because you don't want to draw attention to yourself.
sentences.zh: 有时你甚至会做一些事情，比如身处某种情况，但你表现得比较拘谨，因为你不想引起注意。

sentences.en: So you may feel like you have to change your personality in order to not be the target of anything.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会觉得为了不成为任何人的目标，你必须改变自己的个性。

sentences.en: And when you're changing your thinking or behavior like this and it doesn't feel consistent with who you are, that can lead to experiences of depression or anxiety.
sentences.zh: 当你这样改变自己的思维或行为，而这感觉与真实的你不一致时，这可能会导致抑郁或焦虑。

sentences.en: Certainly it can be stressful and one would experience it as being stress.
sentences.zh: 当然，这可能会让人感到压力，人们也会将其体验为压力。

sentences.en: And stress over time can have a very serious impact on the body.
sentences.zh: 而长期的压力会对身体产生非常严重的影响。

sentences.en: Why is it so important to look at how different groups experience this type of stress?
sentences.zh: 为什么研究不同群体如何体验这种压力如此重要？

sentences.en: We know that different groups report different experiences of stress.
sentences.zh: 我们知道不同群体报告的压力体验是不同的。

sentences.en: They can be stressed about different kinds of topics or they report different levels of stress.
sentences.zh: 他们可能对不同的话题感到压力，或者他们报告的压力水平不同。

sentences.en: But we know less about what these different experiences of stress mean for each of these groups.
sentences.zh: 但我们对这些不同的压力体验对每个群体意味着什么知之甚少。

sentences.en: Does it place certain groups at greater risk for disease?
sentences.zh: 它是否使某些群体面临更大的疾病风险？

sentences.en: Does it lead to certain kinds of behavior patterns that are problematic?
sentences.zh: 它是否会导致某些有问题的行为模式？

sentences.en: There's certainly some evidence that racial and ethnic discrimination places people at greater risk for certain health probleMs. But we know very little
sentences.zh: 当然有一些证据表明，种族和民族歧视使人们面临某些健康问题的更大风险。但我们知之甚少

sentences.en: about how different groups might actually cope with stress, too.
sentences.zh: 关于不同群体实际上是如何应对压力的。

sentences.en: While there's a lot of different individual responses to stress, if there are group differences, we may be able to target interventions and education more effectively.
sentences.zh: 虽然对压力的个体反应有很多不同，但如果存在群体差异，我们也许能更有效地针对性地进行干预和教育。

sentences.en: We might be able to identify key sources of stress and modify those.
sentences.zh: 我们也许能够识别压力的关键来源并加以改善。

sentences.en: When the source of stress is something like discrimination, sure, we want to help people who are being discriminated against figure out how to manage their response.
sentences.zh: 当压力的来源是歧视之类的事情时，当然，我们希望帮助那些受到歧视的人找出如何管理他们反应的方法。

sentences.en: But we also want to think about how do we change the discrimination so that they're not experiencing it.
sentences.zh: 但我们也想考虑如何改变歧视，让他们不再经历这种歧视。

sentences.en: So we do want to understand both what the individual is experiencing, but how groups are experiencing it so we know where to target our efforts.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实既想了解个体正在经历什么，也想了解群体正在经历什么，这样我们才知道努力的方向。

sentences.en: It seems many people are uncomfortable discussing racial differences, especially with children.
sentences.zh: 似乎许多人对讨论种族差异感到不舒服，尤其是在孩子面前。

sentences.en: How can parents and other adults address topics of diversity and discrimination with children of all ages?
sentences.zh: 父母和其他成年人如何与各年龄段的孩子谈论多样性和歧视的话题？

sentences.en: Kids notice differences.
sentences.zh: 孩子们会注意到差异。

sentences.en: They notice when people are treated differently.
sentences.zh: 他们会注意到人们受到不同对待的时候。

sentences.en: And discussing these differences openly in a non-judgmental way allows kids to have the space to ask the questions that they're coming up with.
sentences.zh: 公开地、以非评判的方式讨论这些差异，可以让孩子们有空间去提出他们想到的问题。

sentences.en: And ideally, parents and other adults can help children to value the differences that people have, as well as recognizing what they have in common.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，父母和其他成年人可以帮助孩子重视人们之间的差异，同时认识到他们的共同点。

sentences.en: When adults are going to have these conversations with kids, they need to keep in mind both the age of the child and the developmental stage so they know how best to respond.
sentences.zh: 当成年人要与孩子进行这些对话时，他们需要考虑到孩子的年龄和发展阶段，以便知道如何最好地回应。

sentences.en: Younger children probably need simpler, more basic conversations, but with opportunities to ask questions and talk about things.
sentences.zh: 年幼的孩子可能需要更简单、更基础的对话，但要有机会提问和谈论事情。

sentences.en: Middle school kids, a lot of times information and facts are of a lot of interest to them.
sentences.zh: 对于中学生，很多时候他们对信息和事实非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: With teenagers, you want to have as much opportunity for exploration discussion with them
sentences.zh: 对于青少年，你要尽可能多地为他们提供探索和讨论的机会，

sentences.en: because they're going to have their own ideas and opinions about what's happening and what they've observed.
sentences.zh: 因为他们会对正在发生的事情以及他们观察到的事情有自己的想法和观点。

sentences.en: But at any point, adults should be prepared for surprising or challenging comments or questions.
sentences.zh: 但在任何时候，成年人都应该准备好应对令人惊讶或具有挑战性的评论或问题。

sentences.en: And with any conversation with kids, it's okay to admit our mistakes when perhaps maybe we did
sentences.zh: 在与孩子的任何对话中，承认我们的错误是可以的，比如也许我们确实

sentences.en: treat someone differently or maybe we failed to stand up to an experience of discrimination and we wished we could have done it differently.
sentences.zh: 以不同的方式对待了某人，或者也许我们未能站出来反对歧视经历，而我们希望当时能做得不同。

sentences.en: That can really go a long way in opening a conversation with the child.
sentences.zh: 这对于开启与孩子的对话真的大有帮助。

sentences.en: But I think another question that's important to consider is what if your child is aware of differences and feels like
sentences.zh: 但我认为另一个需要考虑的重要问题是，如果你的孩子意识到差异，并觉得

sentences.en: he or she's being discriminated against or simply being treated differently?
sentences.zh: 他或她受到歧视，或者仅仅是受到不同对待，该怎么办？

sentences.en: It's really important for the adults in their life to acknowledge that that could be their reality.
sentences.zh: 对于他们生活中的成年人来说，承认这可能是他们的现实是非常重要的。

sentences.en: It's appropriate to share your own experiences if you've had such experiences.
sentences.zh: 如果你有过这样的经历，分享你自己的经历是合适的。

sentences.en: You talk about what it means, how your child can respond if that happens again.
sentences.zh: 你要谈论这意味着什么，如果再次发生这种情况，你的孩子可以如何回应。

sentences.en: You don't want to dwell on it, but you certainly don't want to dismiss it either.
sentences.zh: 你不想纠结于此，但你当然也不想忽视它。

sentences.en: In past years, APA's Stress in America survey has consistently concluded that Americans are more stressed about finances than anything else.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，美国心理学会的“美国压力”调查一致得出结论，美国人对财务的压力比其他任何事情都大。

sentences.en: Money continues to be a significant source of stress.
sentences.zh: 金钱仍然是一个重要的压力来源。

sentences.en: Was this consistent in other groups across different groups?
sentences.zh: 这在不同群体中是否一致？

sentences.en: What can people do about money-related stress?
sentences.zh: 人们能为与金钱相关的压力做些什么？

sentences.en: Money has been a significant source of stress in almost every survey we've done over the years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，在我们所做的几乎每一次调查中，金钱都是一个重要的压力来源。

sentences.en: And it doesn't really matter who's responding, whether we divide it by different racial ethnic groups, men and women, if we look at different ages.
sentences.zh: 而且谁在回答并不重要，无论是按不同的种族、民族群体、男女划分，还是看不同的年龄段。

sentences.en: Well, the only time we see money not being a top source of stress, the top source of stress, is with the matures, the oldest demographic in our sample.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们唯一一次看到金钱不是首要压力来源的情况，是在我们样本中最年长的人群中。

sentences.en: And they're more often reporting stress about health concerns.
sentences.zh: 他们更多地报告关于健康问题的压力。

sentences.en: But everyone is talking about money-related stress.
sentences.zh: 但每个人都在谈论与金钱相关的压力。

sentences.en: And sometimes the reality is there just isn't enough money.
sentences.zh: 有时现实情况就是钱不够用。

sentences.en: And when that's the case, figuring out how to get assistance so you can cover the basics, whether you need public
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，弄清楚如何获得援助以满足基本需求，无论你是需要公共

sentences.en: assistance or talking with family or getting loans, that's really important.
sentences.zh: 援助，还是与家人交谈或获得贷款，这真的很重要。

sentences.en: But then the next kind of money stress is sometimes related to what we think we need or what we think we should have.
sentences.zh: 但接下来的那种金钱压力有时与我们认为我们需要什么或我们认为我们应该拥有什么有关。

sentences.en: We might have the money for basics, but we want other things as well.
sentences.zh: 我们可能有基本生活的钱，但我们也想要其他东西。

sentences.en: So then we need to start evaluating how we use and manage money and the choices we make with money.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要开始评估我们如何使用和管理金钱，以及我们在金钱上做出的选择。

sentences.en: Because our perceptions of what we need and want and desire may not match with what we actually have.
sentences.zh: 因为我们对我们需要、想要和渴望的东西的认知可能与我们实际拥有的不匹配。

sentences.en: So shifting our perceptions and trying to understand where we're actually spending our money, how does that fit with what we value, and trying to make those be more consistent.
sentences.zh: 所以改变我们的认知，试着了解我们实际上把钱花在哪里，这与我们重视的东西如何契合，并努力使它们更加一致。

sentences.en: Budgeting is very important when you're talking about, do I have enough money or not?
sentences.zh: 当你谈论我是否有足够的钱时，预算非常重要。

sentences.en: And what is it that I think is needed?
sentences.zh: 我到底认为什么是需要的？

sentences.en: Do I need the luxury car or an economy car?
sentences.zh: 我需要豪华车还是经济型车？

sentences.en: There's choices that we make when people talk about money stress.
sentences.zh: 当人们谈论金钱压力时，我们确实会做出选择。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's about covering the basics, but sometimes it's about what's my status with money and where do I have with it.
sentences.zh: 有时是为了满足基本需求，但有时是关于我在金钱方面的地位以及我拥有什么。

sentences.en: And people have complicated relationships with money.
sentences.zh: 人们与金钱的关系很复杂。

sentences.en: For some individuals, how much they earn has a lot to do with how they feel about themselves and their own personal worth.
sentences.zh: 对于一些人来说，他们赚多少钱与他们如何看待自己和自己的个人价值有很大关系。

sentences.en: And if that's some of the money stress that a person's feeling, they really need to evaluate that and sort of make sure that money's not defining who they are.
sentences.zh: 如果这就是一个人感受到的部分金钱压力，他们真的需要评估这一点，并确保金钱不会定义他们是谁。

sentences.en: Other things that are important to do are talk to family members about the money that you have and the stress you might have about that money.
sentences.zh: 其他重要的事情是与家人谈论你拥有的钱以及你可能对这些钱感到的压力。

sentences.en: Maybe your partner doesn't know the full financial situation.
sentences.zh: 也许你的伴侣不了解全部的财务状况。

sentences.en: Or maybe your kids have unrealistic expectations and make a lot of demands.
sentences.zh: 或者也许你的孩子有不切实际的期望并提出很多要求。

sentences.en: Talk with them about what's reasonable.
sentences.zh: 与他们谈谈什么是合理的。

sentences.en: So it's trying to be more aware of what your financial situation actually is, how that maps on to what your needs and values are, and manage your own
sentences.zh: 所以这是试图更清楚地了解你的财务状况到底是什么，这如何与你的需求和价值观相对应，并管理你自己的

sentences.en: personal expectations about what money means, what money should buy for you to make it more consistent with the money that you have.
sentences.zh: 个人期望，关于金钱意味着什么，金钱应该为你买到什么，以使其与你拥有的金钱更加一致。

sentences.en: But it is tough when you don't have the money for the basics.
sentences.zh: 但当你没有钱满足基本需求时，这确实很艰难。

sentences.en: No doubt about that.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: That is stress.
sentences.zh: 那就是压力。

sentences.en: As a licensed psychologist, you treat people who are dealing with stress of all kinds.
sentences.zh: 作为一名执业心理学家，你治疗各种压力的人。

sentences.en: You talked a little bit about this, but is all stress bad?
sentences.zh: 你刚才谈到了一点，但所有的压力都是坏的吗？

sentences.en: And you know, which is considered bad stress, which is considered good stress?
sentences.zh: 你知道，哪些被认为是坏压力，哪些被认为是好压力？

sentences.en: And what sort of advice do you give to people who are experiencing this high levels of the bad stress?
sentences.zh: 对于那些正在经历高水平坏压力的人，你给他们什么建议？

sentences.en: You know, stress happens all the time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，压力一直都在发生。

sentences.en: We talk in this country about being stressed for everything.
sentences.zh: 我们在这个国家谈论对每件事都感到压力。

sentences.en: Stress can happen.
sentences.zh: 压力可能会发生。

sentences.en: We can be excited about planning a wedding, but feel stressed because of all the pieces we're trying to pull together.
sentences.zh: 我们可能对计划婚礼感到兴奋，但因为我们要处理的所有事情而感到压力。

sentences.en: We might feel stressed about an upcoming exam, but that stress might actually motivate us to study for the exam.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会对即将到来的考试感到压力，但这种压力实际上可能会激励我们为考试而学习。

sentences.en: So those are not necessarily bad stress.
sentences.zh: 所以这些不一定是坏压力。

sentences.en: I think of bad stress as problematic stress as when the demands that you're feeling outmatch your ability to deal with them.
sentences.zh: 我认为坏压力是问题压力，即你感受到的需求超过了你处理它们的能力。

sentences.en: You just don't have the resources to cope with whatever the situation is.
sentences.zh: 你只是没有资源来应对任何情况。

sentences.en: That's when stress is really becoming problematic.
sentences.zh: 那就是压力真正变得有问题的时候。

sentences.en: And when you have that amount of stress where you're feeling that your personal resources, psychological, emotional,
sentences.zh: 当你承受那种程度的压力，感到你的个人资源，心理、情感、

sentences.en: social resources outstrip the demands on your life, a lot of things can happen.
sentences.zh: 社会资源超过了你生活中的需求时，很多事情都会发生。

sentences.en: Physiologically, your body gets more ramped up and you might have more experiences of a racing heart.
sentences.zh: 生理上，你的身体会变得更加亢奋，你可能会有更多心跳加速的体验。

sentences.en: You might have trouble digesting food.
sentences.zh: 你可能会有消化困难。

sentences.en: It can play havoc with your blood sugar.
sentences.zh: 它会扰乱你的血糖。

sentences.en: There's all kinds of physiological changes that can happen.
sentences.zh: 各种生理变化都可能发生。

sentences.en: Muscle tension, all kinds of mental and emotional strain that a person can experience.
sentences.zh: 肌肉紧张，以及一个人可能经历的各种心理和情绪压力。

sentences.en: And when a person gets to that point, reaching out for support.
sentences.zh: 当一个人达到那个点时，寻求支持。

sentences.en: Sometimes it can be support from family or friends, but sometimes you realize I need some support from a professional.
sentences.zh: 有时可以是来自家人或朋友的支持，但有时你会意识到我需要专业人士的支持。

sentences.en: And if I'm seeing somebody who's really struggling with a lot of stress, we talk about how are they thinking about the things in their lives?
sentences.zh: 如果我看到有人真的在承受很大的压力，我们会谈论他们是如何看待生活中的事情的？

sentences.en: Are they filling themselves up with a lot of musts and shoulds and absolutes and things would only be better if, but that if is awfully hard to attain.
sentences.zh: 他们是否用太多的“必须”、“应该”、“绝对”来填满自己，以及事情只有在……的情况下才会更好，但那个“如果”是非常难以实现的。

sentences.en: And we talk about how can we think about the situations in a way that's a little more realistic and less demanding on the person themselves.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论如何以一种更现实、对自己要求更少的方式来看待这些情况。

sentences.en: But we also talk about things like, how do you balance your life?
sentences.zh: 但我们也谈论诸如，你如何平衡你的生活？

sentences.en: Do you know how to say no?
sentences.zh: 你知道如何说不吗？

sentences.en: Do you turn down things that seem to be excessive?
sentences.zh: 你会拒绝那些看起来过分的事情吗？

sentences.en: Do you do things that give you pleasure and help you relax and enjoy?
sentences.zh: 你做那些能给你带来快乐并帮助你放松和享受的事情吗？

sentences.en: You know, I tell new parents a lot of times, if you don't take care of yourself, you can't take care of your child very well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我经常告诉新手父母，如果你不照顾好自己，你就不能很好地照顾你的孩子。

sentences.en: It's important to give yourself some downtime when you can find that in your day.
sentences.zh: 当你能在一天中找到时间时，给自己一些休息时间是很重要的。

sentences.en: And people find that very difficult, but part of what I do is strategize with them about how to do that.
sentences.zh: 人们发现这非常困难，但我工作的一部分是与他们一起制定如何做到这一点的策略。

sentences.en: I worked with somebody who was very stressed with her work situation.
sentences.zh: 我曾与一位对工作状况感到非常压力的人合作。

sentences.en: And we considered three questions.
sentences.zh: 我们考虑了三个问题。

sentences.en: We thought about, could she do something differently in how she responded to the demands in her work?
sentences.zh: 我们思考，她是否可以在应对工作需求的方式上做些不同的事情？

sentences.en: Could she change the demands at her work?
sentences.zh: 她能改变工作中的需求吗？

sentences.en: And ultimately, she decided to go with the third option, which was to leave her work and find a new job.
sentences.zh: 最终，她决定选择第三个方案，即离开她的工作并找一份新工作。

sentences.en: Because she felt she'd done many things to change her responses to the stress.
sentences.zh: 因为她觉得她已经做了很多事情来改变她对压力的反应。

sentences.en: She didn't think she could change the work environment.
sentences.zh: 她认为她无法改变工作环境。

sentences.en: So she determined she needed a new position.
sentences.zh: 所以她决定她需要一个新的职位。

sentences.en: And those are all things we need to think through.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们需要仔细考虑的事情。

sentences.en: Am I responding to stress in a way that is amplifying it?
sentences.zh: 我是否正在以一种放大压力的方式来应对压力？

sentences.en: Or am I managing it in a way that I can let it go and walk away from it at times?
sentences.zh: 或者我是否正在以一种可以放下它并有时远离它的方式来管理它？

sentences.en: Can I change the situation in some way?
sentences.zh: 我能以某种方式改变这种情况吗？

sentences.en: Or do I need to leave the situation in order to be less stressed?
sentences.zh: 或者我需要离开这种情况以减少压力？

sentences.en: And those are all important things to think about.
sentences.zh: 这些都是需要考虑的重要事项。

sentences.en: And they're not easy.
sentences.zh: 而且它们并不容易。

sentences.en: And talking with a professional can help you think through your options and challenge how you're thinking about situations.
sentences.zh: 与专业人士交谈可以帮助你理清思路，并审视你对各种情况的看法。

sentences.en: And also learn things about how to manage the physical changes that can happen with stress.
sentences.zh: 同时也能学习如何应对压力带来的生理变化。

sentences.en: Whether you learn meditation or relaxation.
sentences.zh: 无论是学习冥想还是放松技巧。

sentences.en: Or think about other ways to help your body reduce its responsivity to stress.
sentences.zh: 或者考虑其他能帮助身体降低压力反应的方法。

sentences.en: What can happen if you don't address these issues?
sentences.zh: 如果不去解决这些问题会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: And we're talking about the high levels of bad stress.
sentences.zh: 我们这里指的是高水平的负面压力。

sentences.en: What health implications could be a result of that?
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致什么样的健康后果？

sentences.en: It's interesting on the APA Help Center.
sentences.zh: 在APA帮助中心有一个很有意思的内容。

sentences.en: We have a really neat graphic of a human body.
sentences.zh: 我们有一张非常直观的人体图。

sentences.en: And it shows all the different domains in the body that can be impacted by stress.
sentences.zh: 它展示了人体中所有可能受压力影响的部位。

sentences.en: So a person can, if their body physiologically is being really reactive to stress, the heart rate may go up.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一个人的身体对压力产生了强烈的生理反应，心率可能会升高。

sentences.en: They may be breathing more erratically.
sentences.zh: 他们的呼吸可能会变得不稳定。

sentences.en: They may feel lightheaded because of that.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会因此感到头晕。

sentences.en: They may have muscle tension a lot.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会经常感到肌肉紧张。

sentences.en: So they may feel very stiff and have body aches.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能会感到身体非常僵硬并伴有疼痛。

sentences.en: Their heart may be racing more.
sentences.zh: 他们的心跳可能会加速。

sentences.en: They may have an increase in the stress hormones.
sentences.zh: 他们体内的压力荷尔蒙可能会增加。

sentences.en: You know, the cortisol, which can have an impact on the body over time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是皮质醇，它长期下来会对身体产生影响。

sentences.en: There does seem to be some relationship between chronic physical health conditions and stress, as well as between anxiety and depression and stress.
sentences.zh: 慢性身体健康状况与压力之间，以及焦虑、抑郁与压力之间，似乎确实存在某种关联。

sentences.en: So all of that unchecked over time can have a pretty profound impact on a person's life.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果这些问题长期得不到控制，可能会对一个人的生活产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: Okay, Dr. Bufka, thank you so much for joining us.
sentences.zh: 好的，Bufka博士，非常感谢您参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们的邀请。

sentences.en: To see the latest Stress in America report and to hear more podcast episodes, please go to our website, speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 欲查看最新的《美国压力报告》并收听更多播客节目，请访问我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org。

sentences.en: With the American Psychological Association's
sentences.zh: 这里是美国心理学会的

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology, I'm Audrey Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》，我是Audrey Hamilton。
